subject: Hosted latency handshake + streaming concurrency — Horizon Health follow-up
messages:
From: Emma Colby <emma.colby@horizon-health.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>
Cc: platform@horizon-health.com
Date: Thu, 8 Jul 2027 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Hosted latency check-in & remaining asks

Thanks for the demo earlier — good visibility into the streaming behavior and how Redwood handles prefix caching. A couple of follow-ups from our side so we can close the performance bar for our procurement team:

- Quick recap: our incumbent is currently meeting p95 ~420ms and p99 ~1.6s for end-to-end requests (includes our frontend + network + provider). We surfaced concerns around tail behavior under bursty traffic (concurrency spikes).
- What we need from Redwood: concrete expected hosted numbers for our baseline traffic (details attached), and a test plan we can run during a brief production-shadow window.
- Streaming specifics: we are using chunked responses for user messages (avg token length ~120). We need confirmation on concurrent streaming sessions per replica and an approach to preserve low tail latency when concurrency grows from 50 -> 500 in a 5-minute spike.

Can your team share:
1) an expected p95/p99 E2E envelope for the hosted API for our traffic profile;
2) recommended concurrency and throughput knobs (connection limits, max inflight tokens) for the test;
3) a suggested 2-hour test window (we'd like to schedule next Tue-Wed).

Attaching our exported latency profile (CSV) for the demo baseline.

Thanks,
Emma
Emma Colby
Director, Platform Engineering
Horizon Health

Attachments: horizon_latency_profile.csv (CSV, 78KB)
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>
To: Emma Colby <emma.colby@horizon-health.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 9 Jul 2027 09:38:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted latency check-in & remaining asks

Hi Emma — thanks for the clear notes and the CSV. I copied Ben (seeding the test harness) and Marissa (commercial/SLAs). High-level responses and an actionable plan below.

Quick answers up front:
- Baseline expected E2E (hosted API) for your traffic profile: p95 ≈ 210–280 ms; p99 ≈ 650–820 ms. Those ranges assume we enable lightweight KV-prefix caching and run with our streaming-aware kernel path.
- Concurrency guidance: we recommend starting tests at a concurrency cap of 200 concurrent streams per replica, with autoscale to allow an additional 3x burst (so replicas scale to handle ~600). For the shadow window we suggest a capped burst to 500 to reproduce your worst-case.
- Throughput knobs: set request-level inflight token limit to 256 and enable persistent connections for the longest-lived client flows.

Proposed test plan (attached): rdw_streaming_test_plan.pdf (short checklist + harness commands). High-level timeline:
1) Day 0 prep: we sync on model variant and deploy test harness in shadow mode (no user-facing traffic).
2) 2-hour shadow window: 30 min ramp, 60 min steady at target envelope, 30 min burst exercise (step up to 500 conc).
3) Post-run triage: collect p95/p99, CPU/GPU per-replica, and kernel-level logs.

Can you confirm next Tue (2027-07-13) 11:00 PT for a 30-minute handoff? If that works we will provision a dedicated test lane and share the runbook + a temporary API key.

Attaching: rdw_streaming_test_plan.pdf (PDF, 240KB) and a short mapping CSV we used to translate frontend timings to our probe timings.

Best,
Jasmine Liu
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: rdw_streaming_test_plan.pdf (PDF, 240KB)
From: Emma Colby <emma.colby@horizon-health.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>
Cc: platform@horizon-health.com, Diego Alvarez <diego.alvarez@horizon-health.com>
Date: Fri, 9 Jul 2027 10:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted latency check-in & remaining asks

Thanks Jasmine — those numbers look promising. A couple of clarifying points before we lock a test window:

- Model variant: our production uses a quantized 13B variant with half-precision optimizations. Does Redwood have a pre-quantized artifact that matches our variant, or will we run an equivalent unquantized one for the probe?
- SLA ask: procurement wants a p99 commitment under 700 ms for the hosted lane (we understand this is ambitious). Can you indicate whether that can be accommodated as a trial SLA for the POC period?

I'll confirm Tue 11:00 PT if Diego is available for the ramp details.

—Emma
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Emma Colby <emma.colby@horizon-health.com>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 10 Jul 2027 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted latency check-in & remaining asks

Emma — quick technical clarifications from the serving/runtime side so you have a concrete proposal for the test and the POC SLA conversation: 

1) Quantization & model parity: We support loading 13B quantized weights (8-bit/4-bit depending on artifact). For an apples-to-apples probe we can deploy your quantized artifact (you'd provide the artifact or we can perform a quick quantization step with your consent).

2) Expected envelope (targeted test config):
   - Replica config: 1x A100-equivalent per replica, streaming-optimized kernel path enabled.
   - Client-side steady envelope: 200 concurrent streams, mean tokens/window 120.
   - Measured (hosted probe, shadow mode): p95 ≈ 230 ms, p99 ≈ 680 ms.

3) Tail behavior & mitigation: p99 is sensitive to cold KV-cache misses and cold-start inflight compilation. Our suggested mitigations for the burst window:
   - Pre-warm KV cache with a short prefix sweep during the ramp phase.
   - Apply a soft concurrency queue at the ingress layer to smooth instantaneous spikes above replica capacity.
   - Enable one-shot fallback to a cheaper model variant for the 1–2% of requests that exceed 1.5s under stress.

4) POC SLA: For the POC window (4 weeks), we can offer a trial SLA target of p99 < 700 ms for the hosted lane, with two caveats: (a) it applies to the monitored E2E envelope defined in our runbook; (b) any production cutover will need a 2-week stabilization period and an agreed runbook for failover to the incumbent. Marissa — can you prepare a short commercial note for procurement on that conditional SLA?

Next steps: Jasmine to share the temporary API key and runbook link once Tue 11:00 PT is confirmed. If Diego confirms model artifact handoff, we can schedule an earlier prep pass on Mon afternoon.

– Ben
Principal Performance Engineer
Redwood Inference
